shouldFix.title: The per-generation finding record is not keyed consistently under any single reading, and the structured register remains five rounds stale, so generation-level accounting still cannot be relied on
evidence: The four generation keys hold nine entries: honestyRepairsFromV9 = [HAE9-CX-01, CLAUDE-HEA9-S1]; honestyRepairsFromV10 = [HAE10-CX-01]; honestyRepairsFromV11 = [HAE11-CX-01, IR-HEA10-B1, IR-HEA10-S2]; honestyRepairsFromV12 = [HAE12-CX-01, HAE12-CX-02, CLAUDE-HEA11-S3].

Read as 'findings raised against version N', which is the reading honestyRepairsFromV9 and V10 satisfy exactly, three entries are misfiled: IR-HEA10-B1 and IR-HEA10-S2 were raised in the v10 review and sit under V11, and CLAUDE-HEA11-S3 was raised in my v11 review and sits under V12.

Read as 'repairs performed in version N+1', which V10, V11 and V12 all satisfy, one entry is misfiled: CLAUDE-HEA9-S1 sits under V9 but was repaired at v11, not v10, as the v11 artifact and my frozen v11 verdict both record. HAE9-CX-01 under the same key was repaired at v10.
So no single reading makes all four keys consistent, and the inconsistent entry under the second reading is the very entry v13 added to satisfy CLAUDE-HEA11-S3.

The practical consequence is the one S3 existed to prevent. A reader asking 'were all findings raised against v11 addressed?' opens honestyRepairsFromV11, finds HAE11-CX-01 plus two v10-round items, and does not find CLAUDE-HEA11-S3, which is filed a generation later.

The structured register is unchanged and now five rounds stale. predecessorVerdictFindings still has top-level keys ['prior','v6','v7'] and records rounds v1 through v7 only, each with verdict, pinned verdict digest and per-finding dispositions. There is no v8, v9, v10, v11 or v12 entry, so neither the v8 dual ACCEPT that underlies the D-093 recording nor any verdict from the five rounds since is recorded there.

The omission is unmanaged rather than deliberate. The string predecessorVerdictFindings occurs exactly once in the 87309-byte subject, as its own key, and no note anywhere states that the register is capped at v7 or superseded by the honestyRepairsFrom* chain.

Extending that register was the second clause of my v11 requiredRepair, which read in part 'Extend predecessorVerdictFindings with v8, v9 and v10 rounds in the shape already used for v6 and v7, each naming the verdict, the pinned digest, and per-finding dispositions.' v13's repair note for CLAUDE-HEA11-S3 addresses only the honestyRepairsFromV9 clause and is silent on this one.
shouldFix.impact: Generation-level accounting is the mechanism by which each successor reviewer checks that every finding of the preceding round was addressed and that none was quietly dropped. With the keys inconsistent in both directions and the register stale since v7, that check cannot be performed from the artifact alone: a reviewer must already know each finding's id to locate it, which defeats the purpose of a per-generation record. This is a narrowed successor to CLAUDE-HEA11-S3 rather than a re-assertion of it, because the substantive harm I reported at v11, a finding with zero occurrences anywhere in the subject, is genuinely cured: all nine finding ids from v9 onward now appear with their repairs described, and honestyRepairsFromV12[2] states the governing rule that replacing a repair record is not a withdrawal.
shouldFix.requiredRepair: Pick one reading of the honestyRepairsFromVN key, state it once in the artifact, and refile the entries that violate it. If the key means findings raised against vN, move IR-HEA10-B1 and IR-HEA10-S2 to honestyRepairsFromV10 and CLAUDE-HEA11-S3 to honestyRepairsFromV11. If it means repairs performed in vN+1, move CLAUDE-HEA9-S1 to honestyRepairsFromV10. Separately, either extend predecessorVerdictFindings with the v8 through v12 rounds in the shape already used for v6 and v7, each naming the verdict, the pinned verdict digest and per-finding dispositions, or add an explicit note recording that the register is closed at v7 and that the honestyRepairsFrom* chain supersedes it from v8 onward. Leaving it silently unmaintained is the one option that keeps the ambiguity.

verdictBasis: The dispatch permits ACCEPT only at 0 blockers and 0 SHOULD-FIX. This review returns 0 blockers and 1 SHOULD-FIX, so the verdict is REJECT. This is the strongest generation of this lineage I have seen. Codex's HAE12-CX-01 blocker is repaired on both clauses with the mapping's 19/19 totality restored and verified mechanically; HAE12-CX-02 is repaired and I confirmed the corrected digest attribution against git history rather than the artifact's narration, finding 54d34099 at the D-032 commit and 7c6d8a56 at the D-037 commit exactly as claimed; my own S1 and S2 from v11 are repaired and have not regressed; and the substantive harm of S3, a finding with no trace anywhere in the artifact, is genuinely cured. The single remaining finding is narrow: the per-generation repair record is keyed inconsistently under both available readings of its own key, with the offending entry under one reading being the very entry added to satisfy S3, and the structured register that was supposed to carry this accounting is still five rounds stale with no note explaining why. Because generation-level accounting is what lets each successor reviewer verify that nothing was dropped, and because that is precisely what S3 was about, it does not clear the bar. It is repairable by refiling three entries and either extending or explicitly closing one register.
